title: OM651 / CRD3-MFA1 12 V energy management (AGK): battery readings and the battery-change routines
notes: On the MFA platform (W117 CLA, W176 A, X156 GLA) the 12 V energy manager lives INSIDE the engine ECU (CRD3-MFA1, 0x7E0/0x7E8). There is no separate battery-management module to reach. The IBS current sensor (0x74F/0x757 on the 125k chassis CAN, and 0x6D5/0x6B0) carries F1xx identification only -- no registration.
The classic Mercedes rear-SAM 'Batteriewechsel' write (DID 0x0562, charge-balance index) belongs to W204/W212/W231. It does NOT exist on this platform.
None of these routines needs SecurityAccess: the mined per-service security level is 0 for 03A0, 03A1, 03A2, 03A3, 03A7 and 035B. The extended session 10 03 is enough.

Every parameter in the CBF declares BigEndian, and that field has already been proven a lie on another Mercedes ECU. Decodes here are big-endian because that is all the corpus offers; the raw bytes are always kept so a wrong decode can be re-read, not re-driven.

The CBF names every routine input parameter 'Injektorcode' regardless of what it really is, so the input MEANINGS below are inference from the routine name plus the read-back DIDs, not mined fact. They are labelled as such.

ON-CAR VERDICT, W117 CLA 220 CDI (WDD1179032N291528), 2026-09-09: this ECU's energy-management block is NOT LIVE. Every channel returns the same bytes with the ignition on, the engine off and the engine running at 766 rpm -- capacity 0, current exactly 0.0 A, SOC exactly 60 %, temperature exactly 30.0 degC, measurement state 0 -- while rpm (5017) and rail pressure (D058) from the same ECU in the same session move normally. A running engine must show charging current and about 14 V, so these are placeholders, not readings. Routines 03A0 and 03A2 both returned POSITIVE (7101 03A0 / 7101 03A2), so the ECU accepts them; they simply write into a function this car's calibration does not run. Conclusion: there is nothing to register on this variant, and a positive reply here does not mean a registration took effect. Always read 6153/6161/6165 before and after and believe the read, not the acknowledgement.

readings.label: Latched battery capacity (ESOC_CapaHV_Mem)
readings.why: The capacity the energy manager is currently working to. This is the number a registration changes.

readings.label: Current maximum available capacity
readings.why: What the ECU believes the battery can actually hold right now, after ageing.

readings.label: Calculated maximum available capacity (from the last battery measurement)
readings.why: The ECU's own measured answer. If this tracks the new battery, the ECU is self-learning and a capacity write is not needed.

readings.label: State of charge (SOC)
readings.why: Straight after a battery change this is usually wrong until the ECU re-measures.

readings.label: Battery voltage (BMS_Batt_Volt)
readings.why: The energy manager's own voltage. The mined multiplier 0.0625 gives 118.75 V, which no 12 V system can sit at, so it is corrected by a decade here on physical grounds. That correction is NOT confirmed against a known voltage: on the CLA the channel is frozen at 0x076C engine off and engine running alike, so it carried no live value to check against. Confirm on a car whose block is live.

readings.label: Battery current (BMS_Batt_Curr)
readings.why: Positive = charging. This is the IBS sensor's reading arriving at the engine ECU.

readings.label: Battery temperature (BMS_Batt_Temp)
readings.why: Charging voltage is temperature compensated; a silly temperature means the IBS is not being believed.

readings.label: SOC status bits (summary)
readings.why: Bit meanings are not mined. Kept raw so a before/after change is still visible.

readings.label: Battery measurement function state
readings.why: Says whether the ECU's own capacity measurement (routine 035B) has run.

readings.label: Start battery voltage for battery measurement
readings.why: Latched start voltage. Reads 0x2ED3 on this car on every read across four separate days. CORRECTED 2026-09-09: the mined multiplier 0.01 gives 119.87 V; a tenth of it gives 11.987 V, which is a believable resting voltage -- so the value was always plausible and it is the scaling, not the channel, that was wrong. It is still suspiciously constant, so treat it as latched rather than live.

currentless.title: Set or Reset Currentless Condition
currentless.why: Tells the 12 V energy manager that the car was disconnected from its battery. That is exactly what happened when the battery was swapped. It resets the charge-balance history so the manager stops applying the old battery's learned state to the new one. This is the conservative half of a Mercedes battery registration: it changes bookkeeping, not the battery model.
currentless.input_note: One input byte, mined default 0x00. The CBF mislabels it 'Injektorcode' so the set/reset sense of 0x00 vs 0x01 is NOT mined fact. The mined default is sent unchanged; nothing is invented.

set_capacity.title: Set Battery Capacity
set_capacity.why: Writes the commanded battery capacity into the energy manager. Only needed when the new battery's capacity differs from the old one.
set_capacity.input_note: Four payload bytes. The CBF declares ONE 16-bit input at byte offset 4 and says nothing about bytes 6-7 or about scaling. The scaling used here (ampere-seconds divided by 10, matching read-back DID 6701) is INFERENCE, not mined fact. Never send this without reading 6153/6154/6701 first and again afterwards.

set_ocv.title: Set OCV Characteristic
set_ocv.why: 21 x uint16 at 10 mV resolution, in 5 % state-of-charge steps: the open-circuit-voltage curve that tells the energy manager what CHEMISTRY the battery is (AGM vs flooded). There is no separate battery-type byte anywhere on this platform -- this curve is the type.
set_ocv.input_note: BLOCKED in this harness. The mined payload is 42 zero bytes, which would write a curve of all zeros and destroy the battery model. No correct AGM curve exists in the mined corpus. Read the live curve with 226169 and keep it; do not write one.

measure.title: Battery Measurement Diagnostic
measure.why: The ECU measures the battery's own capacity and internal resistance. This is the self-learning path: if it runs and DID 6701 then reports the new battery, no capacity write is needed at all.
